answer: Shale keeps its history in countable layers, and so should a ballot. Each vertex earns its vote laying shale, one stratum of attested work a day, counted like varves: Lake Suigetsu counts 52,800. A farm of clones fails the strata check: a vertex under twelve layers, or strata matching another's, burns. A trust pulse then walks the graph SybilRank-style — short random walks, O(log n) steps — and ballots it never reaches don't count. Forging 10,000 ballots needs 120,000 strata, $25 staked each, $250,000 frozen. A farm prints 10,000 names overnight; it cannot print 120,000 tides of shale.
